Bound how long an asynchronous call can take

Source: R/async_timeout.R
async_timeout.Rd

Asynchronous version of timeout(), for functions that return a promise. If the promise has not settled after seconds, the promise returned by the decorated function rejects with a fnware_timeout_error, so async_retry() retries it.

Usage

async_timeout(f, seconds, method = async_timeout_later())

async_timeout_base()

async_timeout_fn(class, call, seconds, ...)

async_timeout_later()

Arguments

f

The function to decorate. Usually supplied by %@% rather than directly.

seconds

Time limit for one call, in seconds. A number greater than 0.

method

How to enforce the limit, e.g. async_timeout_later().

class

An async timeout method object, which methods dispatch on.

call

A function of no arguments that starts the work and returns a promise.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

async_timeout() returns a decorator whose decorated function returns a promise. async_timeout_later() returns a method, and async_timeout_fn() returns a promise.

Details

The wrapped function may return a promise or a plain value. A thrown error rejects the promise. Limits:

  • It does not stop the work. The caller is told, but the underlying request or task keeps running. A custom method can cancel it.

  • It cannot bound a function that blocks the session before returning its promise, as the timer needs the event loop. Use timeout() for that.

  • Nested async_timeout()s each run their own timer, so the soonest rejects first. There is no shared deadline like timeout_remaining().

Needs the promises and later packages, and an event loop.

Timeout methods

method decides how the limit is enforced. async_timeout_later(), the only built-in, races the promise against a later::later() timer. To write your own, make an S7 class inheriting from async_timeout_base and register a method for async_timeout_fn(class, call, seconds). call() starts the work and returns a promise. The method must return a promise that settles with its result, or rejects with a fnware_timeout_error once seconds pass. async_timeout() adds the function name and limit, and signals a fnware_timeout_method_error if the method does not return a promise.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# A stand-in for a slow request: resolves after `delay` seconds
slow_request <- function(delay) {
  promises::promise(function(resolve, reject) {
    later::later(function() resolve("response"), delay)
  })
}

f := async_timeout(0.1) %@% slow_request
promises::then(
  f(1),
  onFulfilled = function(value) cat("got", value, "\n"),
  onRejected = function(err) cat("failed:", conditionMessage(err), "\n")
)
while (!later::loop_empty()) later::run_now(0.1)

# Cap each attempt of an async_retry()
fetch := async_retry(stop = stop_after_attempt(3), wait = wait_exp()) %@%
  async_timeout(5) %@%
  function(url) slow_request(1)
} # }
